name: Carroll Street Bridge
facts: The Carroll Street Bridge, completed in 1889, is the oldest surviving retractable bridge in the United States, a rare engineering marvel that slides diagonally on timber‑supported rails to open a 36‑foot channel for canal traffic.

Designed by chief engineer Robert Van Buren and built by Cooper, Hewitt & Company, the bridge’s bright blue trapezoidal span was originally powered by steam, then converted to electric motors in 1908.
After a 1985 mechanical failure left it stuck open for years, the bridge gained landmark status in 1987, was restored in 1989, and survived Hurricane Sandy damage in 2012 before its 2026 reopening.
